chosen.premise: Sandslash can lose its claws and spikes, yet they grow back the very next day.
chosen.hook: What if breaking your claws was only a one-day problem?
chosen.visualIdea: Show Sandslash's claws snapping off, then restore them with a next-day calendar flip.
chosen.note: A highly specific regeneration rule, directly supported by multiple Pokédex entries and easy to dramatize with a break-and-next-day visual.

candidates.premise: Broken Sandslash claws and horns are hard enough to be carved into plows for farm fields.
candidates.hook: Sandslash's broken claws can become farming tools.
candidates.visualIdea: Transform a dropped claw into a plow carving lines through a field.
candidates.note: An unusually specific transformation with a strong contradiction—broken body parts become useful farm tools—and direct Pokédex support.

candidates.premise: Sandslash climbs trees, curls into a spiny ball, and attacks prey by dropping from above.
candidates.hook: Sandslash does not just roll at prey—it drops on it.
candidates.visualIdea: Track Sandslash clawing up a tree, then cut to its spiny-ball drop onto a target below.
candidates.note: A concrete and cinematic hunting tactic, clearly supported by entries describing tree climbing, curling, and dropping onto prey.

candidates.premise: Alolan Sandslash is Ice and Steel, stands 0.2 meters taller, and weighs 25.5 kilograms more.
candidates.hook: Sandslash gets taller, heavier, and turns into Ice and Steel.
candidates.visualIdea: Split-screen the two forms with height and weight counters changing beside their type labels.
candidates.note: The measurements and typing are precise and easy to display, but regional-form comparisons are a broadly reusable angle.

candidates.premise: To hide, Sandslash runs at top speed and kicks up a blinding dust storm around itself.
candidates.hook: Sandslash hides by turning its escape into a dust storm.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Sandslash sprinting across dry ground as the dust cloud grows until it vanishes.
candidates.note: Well supported and visually clear, but the hiding-by-dust concept is less surprising and less distinctive than Sandslash’s regeneration.

candidates.premise: Its spikes are hardened hide, and Sandslash replaces the entire outer layer once every year.
candidates.hook: Sandslash sheds its armor—but only once a year.
candidates.visualIdea: Zoom from a spike's armored texture to old spikes falling away and new ones growing underneath.
candidates.note: The yearly spike replacement is compelling, but “entire outer layer” overstates the evidence, which specifically says the old spikes fall out.

rounds.request: None; one-day-claws is strong enough to lead the episode. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific, surprising rule with direct support and a clear visual payoff.
